contradiction.asr_checkpoint_statement: The official Qwen3-ASR source pin establishes vLLM as the official streaming backend and leaves alternative non-vLLM streaming/timestamp implementations unproven outside that inspected official runtime.
contradiction.cross_lane_evidence_already_present: The prior T7-SYS-004 audio.cpp v0.7.0 source audit already recorded Qwen3-ASR-0.6B/1.7B as German-capable GGUF 16/Q8 Stream candidates.
contradiction.resolution: The stronger project-level statement that no source-pinned non-vLLM streaming path was known is stale. audio.cpp is an admitted non-vLLM C++/ggml/GGUF Qwen3-ASR streaming challenger at source scope. This does not change any target-runtime credit.

upstream_pin.license: Apache-2.0 runtime; model/artifact licenses remain separately binding

source_findings: Current audio.cpp source accepts Qwen3-ASR sessions in both offline and streaming run modes.
Current model documentation states that streaming mode accepts live audio chunks and emits buffered transcript deltas.
Word timestamps are implemented by passing the recognized transcript through Qwen3 Forced Aligner.

Timestamp output remains offline-only because alignment runs after the full transcript is known; therefore native streaming transcript support must not be conflated with streaming word-timestamp support.
Current source exposes Qwen3-ASR weight-type/resource controls and GGUF-oriented deployment paths, making it a materially different runtime hypothesis from the official vLLM streaming path.

Upstream commit 4d383be1 reports a previously observed concurrent-load VRAM failure for Qwen3-ASR-0.6B Q8 on a 12 GB H100L slice and a source fix; this is upstream hardware evidence only and is a warning to measure concurrency/residency on clay-direct-dev rather than assuming stability.
hypothesis_update: For Frankenstein, audio.cpp is now the strongest source-pinned non-vLLM Qwen3-ASR streaming challenger because it preserves a C++/ggml/GGUF path and explicit streaming lifecycle. It may reduce Python/vLLM framework overhead, but that benefit remains unmeasured on the target host.
counterhypothesis: On clay-direct-dev, audio.cpp may still lose to the admitted Whisper/faster-whisper or other ASR paths on German WER/CER, endpoint latency, p95/p99, resident VRAM/RSS, cancellation semantics, or ASR+LLM+TTS coexistence. Offline-only timestamp alignment may also be insufficient for any design that requires live word timing.
